install: Add to the project's Python dependency file (pyproject/requirements) with a pinned, reviewed version and lock it.

items.name: pypdf
items.summary: Pure-Python PDF library to split, merge, crop, encrypt and read text and metadata.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing PDF merge/split, form filling or metadata edits in Python.
cautions: Text extraction quality varies; use pdfplumber for layout-aware extraction.
Malformed PDFs can be slow; set limits for untrusted input.
install: Add to the project's Python dependency file (pyproject/requirements) with a pinned, reviewed version and lock it.

items.name: pdfplumber
items.summary: Python tool for layout-aware PDF text, character and table extraction.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing coordinate-based table extraction from digital PDFs like statements and invoices.
cautions: Works on digital PDFs only; scanned pages need OCR (OCRmyPDF/Tesseract) first.
install: Add to the project's Python dependency file (pyproject/requirements) with a pinned, reviewed version and lock it.

items.name: ReportLab

license.scope: BSD license for the open-source ReportLab Toolkit; ReportLab PLUS/RML products are commercial.

items.summary: Python library for programmatic PDF generation with flowable layouts, tables and charts.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing PDF drawing code for Python-generated reports, invoices and statements.
cautions: Source is hosted on ReportLab's own Mercurial server, not GitHub.
RML templating needs the commercial product.
install: Add to the project's Python dependency file (pyproject/requirements) with a pinned, reviewed version and lock it.

items.name: WeasyPrint
items.summary: Converts HTML and CSS (including paged media) to PDF in Python without a browser.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-laying out PDFs when templates are easier to write in HTML/CSS.
cautions: No JavaScript execution; render dynamic content server-side first.
Needs Pango system libraries; check container images.
install: Add to the project's Python dependency file (pyproject/requirements) with a pinned, reviewed version and lock it.

items.name: Gotenberg

license.scope: MIT for Gotenberg; bundles Chromium and LibreOffice under their own licenses.

items.summary: Docker-based API for converting HTML, Markdown and Office documents to PDF via Chromium and LibreOffice.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-managing headless Chromium/LibreOffice processes for document-to-PDF conversion.
cautions: Keep it on a private network; rendering arbitrary URLs can enable SSRF.
Resource-heavy; set timeouts and concurrency limits.
install: Run the official gotenberg/gotenberg image at a pinned tag as an internal service.

items.name: Pandoc

license.scope: GPL-2.0-or-later. Invoking the CLI as a separate process is common; linking the Haskell library or redistributing binaries needs license review.

items.summary: Universal document converter between Markdown, DOCX, HTML, LaTeX, EPUB, ODT and more.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing format converters between Markdown, Word, HTML and LaTeX.
cautions: Lua filters and some input formats can read files; sandbox untrusted documents (--sandbox).
PDF output needs a LaTeX engine or other PDF engine installed.
install: Install a pinned release binary or the pandoc/core Docker image and invoke it as a subprocess.

items.name: docx (npm)
items.summary: Declarative TypeScript API to generate .docx Word documents in Node or the browser.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing OOXML to generate Word reports, letters or contracts.
cautions: Generation only; it does not edit existing documents in place.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: Mammoth

license.scope: BSD-2-Clause for the JS and Python implementations.

items.summary: Converts .docx to clean semantic HTML or Markdown using style mappings (JS and Python).
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-parsing DOCX XML to import Word content into a CMS or knowledge base.
cautions: Intentionally drops visual formatting; not a fidelity-preserving converter.
Sanitize output HTML before rendering.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: python-docx
items.summary: Python library to create and edit .docx files: paragraphs, tables, styles and images.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-editing OOXML to generate or modify Word documents in Python.
cautions: Limited support for complex features (tracked changes, some field types); verify output in Word.
install: Add to the project's Python dependency file (pyproject/requirements) with a pinned, reviewed version and lock it.

items.name: docxtemplater

license.scope: MIT for the open-source core; many modules (images, HTML, charts) are paid commercial add-ons.

items.summary: Template engine that fills {placeholders}, loops and conditions in DOCX/PPTX/XLSX templates.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-replacing text in OOXML to produce contracts, letters or invoices from Word templates.
cautions: Check whether needed features are in paid modules before committing to it.
Template authors can break tags with Word formatting; validate templates.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: ExcelJS
items.summary: Read, write and style .xlsx workbooks in Node and the browser, including streaming writes.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing XLSX XML to export styled spreadsheets with formulas.
cautions: Release cadence has slowed (last npm release 4.4.0); review open issues before adoption.
Formulas are written, not calculated; Excel recalculates on open.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: SheetJS Community Edition

license.scope: Apache-2.0 for Community Edition; SheetJS Pro is commercial. The npm 'xlsx' package is stale (0.18.5) with known advisories; current builds are distributed from cdn.sheetjs.com.

items.summary: Spreadsheet parser and writer supporting XLSX, XLS, CSV, ODS and many legacy formats.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing parsers for many spreadsheet formats; install from the official CDN tarball, not npm 'xlsx'.
cautions: Do not install the outdated npm 'xlsx' release; pin the CDN tarball URL and integrity.
Styling and some features are Pro-only.
install: Install from the version-pinned tarball documented at docs.sheetjs.com (e.g. https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-<version>/xlsx-<version>.tgz) and commit the lockfile.

items.name: openpyxl
items.summary: Python library to read and write Excel .xlsx files, styles, charts and formulas.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing XLSX XML to read or edit existing workbooks in Python.
cautions: Does not evaluate formulas; cached values may be stale.
Macros and some objects are lost on save; preserve originals.
install: Add to the project's Python dependency file (pyproject/requirements) with a pinned, reviewed version and lock it.

items.name: XlsxWriter
items.summary: Python module for writing richly formatted .xlsx files with charts, formulas and conditional formats.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing styled Excel exports and native charts from Python.
cautions: Write-only; cannot read or modify existing files.
install: Add to the project's Python dependency file (pyproject/requirements) with a pinned, reviewed version and lock it.

items.name: rust_xlsxwriter
items.summary: Rust port of XlsxWriter for writing formatted .xlsx files with charts and tables.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing XLSX XML from Rust services or CLIs.
cautions: Write-only; use calamine to read spreadsheets in Rust.
install: Add with cargo add rust_xlsxwriter and commit Cargo.lock.

items.name: Excelize
items.summary: Go library to read, write and style XLSX/XLSM files including charts, pivot tables and streaming.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing OOXML spreadsheet handling in Go services.
cautions: Formula calculation support is partial; verify computed values.
install: Add with go get github.com/xuri/excelize/v2@<version> and commit go.sum.

items.name: python-pptx
items.summary: Python library to create and modify PowerPoint .pptx files: slides, text, tables, charts and images.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing PresentationML to generate editable slide decks from data.
cautions: Releases are infrequent; complex features (animations, SmartArt) are unsupported.
install: Add to the project's Python dependency file (pyproject/requirements) with a pinned, reviewed version and lock it.

items.name: PptxGenJS
items.summary: JavaScript library to generate PowerPoint presentations with native charts, tables and images.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-writing PresentationML to export editable decks from a web app or Node.
cautions: Generation only; cannot open and edit existing decks.
install: Install with the project's package manager and commit the lockfile; pin the reviewed version.

items.name: LibreOffice (headless)

license.scope: MPL-2.0 for most code, with some components under other licenses; review when redistributing.

items.summary: Open-source office suite whose headless mode converts DOCX/XLSX/PPTX/ODF to PDF and other formats.
items.useWhen: Use instead of writing your own Office-format renderer when you need faithful document-to-PDF conversion.
cautions: Headless conversions are single-threaded per profile; isolate and time-limit processes.
Never enable macros on untrusted documents.
install: Install the distribution package or official build at a pinned version in the container; run soffice --headless --convert-to as a sandboxed subprocess.

items.name: Tesseract OCR

license.scope: Apache-2.0 for the engine; trained data files are separately distributed.

items.summary: Open-source OCR engine with LSTM models for 100+ languages; also available in the browser via tesseract.js.
items.useWhen: Use instead of building text recognition for scanned images and documents.
cautions: Accuracy depends on preprocessing (deskew, binarize, DPI); validate on real samples.
OCR output is not ground truth; keep confidence and human review for critical data.
install: Install the engine from the OS package manager at a pinned version with required language data; for JS use the pinned tesseract.js package.

items.name: OCRmyPDF

license.scope: MPL-2.0 for OCRmyPDF; depends on Tesseract and Ghostscript (AGPL) installed separately.

items.summary: Adds a searchable text layer to scanned PDFs using Tesseract, producing PDF/A output.
items.useWhen: Use instead of hand-wiring Tesseract, image cleanup and PDF assembly for scanned documents.
cautions: Ghostscript is AGPL; review distribution if you bundle it.
Processing is CPU-heavy; queue jobs and set timeouts.
install: Add to the project's Python dependency file (pyproject/requirements) with a pinned, reviewed version and lock it.
